task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
Which comparator defines the 'closest' teammate: profile similarity, minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes? The question lists these as alternatives without choosing one.
With 11 cases and 148 spells, is there enough independent information to test redistribution?
How should regression to the mean and non-random absence selection be handled when measuring gains?
Are the play-type initiation labels and the pre-absence profile derived from the same play-by-play used for the outcome, and does that create circularity?
evidence_establishes: retrieve_history returned no records (n_results=0), so no prior study by this project on this question or on closely related absence-redistribution questions is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer. No earlier result exists to support, reject, or qualify this claim.
Whether any absence-redistribution pattern exists in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data.
Whether the derived play-type labels are valid or reliable.
own_inferences: The effective sample is about 11 independent cases. The 148 spells are nested within those cases, so spell-level counts overstate the information available.

The question's comparator is underspecified. Four candidate rules (profile similarity, total minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) produce different 'closest' teammates, so the test has no single pre-specified prediction.
Absences are probably selected for injury or rest, and players who are absent often have unusual usage before absence. Measured gains could reflect regression to the mean rather than reorganization.

If the pre-absence profile is built from play-by-play that also generates the outcome play-type records, the label and the predictor share a source. This is a risk of circularity and of mechanical correlation.
The 2025-26 playoff data is partial before 2026-06-21, so including it on 2026-11-01 would mix complete and incomplete seasons unless the cutoff is enforced.
uncertainties: No historical records were returned, so the prior-work and failed-approach fields are empty and nothing is known about earlier attempts.
The distribution of absence lengths, the number of primary play types per absent player, and how many cases have a clearly identifiable closest teammate are unknown.
The data catalog and glossary were not consulted, so the exact definitions of initiator and play type were not confirmed.
Whether the 148 spells include multiple absences for the same player is not stated.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so no earlier findings or failed approaches could inform the decision. The decision rests on the design constraints in the task itself: 11 cases, an underspecified comparator, probable selection and regression-to-the-mean effects, and possible label circularity.

blocking_constraints.text: Eleven cases give very little power to detect a teammate-level redistribution effect, especially when the comparator is chosen after seeing the data.

Play-type initiation labels are derived from play-by-play. The same derivation may define both the pre-absence profile and the post-absence gains, so the outcome label is not independent of the predictor.
Absences are not randomly assigned. Players with extreme pre-absence usage can show apparent gains for teammates through regression to the mean alone.
If the 'pre-absence' profile is computed from windows that overlap the absence, or from data made available only after the absence, the test uses future information.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. The decision does not depend on prior work being available.

risks.text: Only 11 cases. Spells are not independent units, so the effective sample is far smaller than 148.
Per-player play-type initiation shares in small pre-absence windows are noisy, so the 'closest profile' ranking may be unstable.
Many primary play types may have very few initiations per player per spell, making gains near zero or undefined for many teammates.
Absences chosen because of unusual usage produce gains that revert without any reorganization.
Concurrent changes in lineup, coach, starters, opponent strength, and minutes distribution can drive gains, and these are not separated from the absence.
Both the profile and the gain depend on the same derived play-type labels, creating circularity.
The play-type and initiator attribution may misassign possessions, particularly in sub-type ambiguous cases.
Pre-absence profiles must be built only from games before the absence start. Overlapping windows would leak post-absence information.
Four comparator definitions and several play types create many implicit tests, so the best-looking one is likely to be a false positive.
Without placebo absences, a gain could be a general feature of teammate usage changes rather than a reorganization response.
The 2025-26 playoff data is partial before 2026-06-21, and team rosters and styles change across 2022-23 to 2025-26.
Most absences may produce no clear largest gainer, so the predicted positive pattern is rare and needs a large sample to detect.

design.estimand: Not specified as posed. A minimum viable estimand is the difference in per-possession change in primary-play-type initiations for the teammate ranked closest on a single pre-registered profile metric, compared with other teammates, after an absence starts, relative to matched non-absence windows.
design.unit: Absence case (player-absence episode), with teammate-by-play-type gains as the within-case observations. The case is the independent unit; spells are nested inside cases.
design.sample: 11 cases from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season. Playoffs are excluded unless the 2025-26 playoff data is confirmed complete at analysis time. Requires a pre-registered list of which of the 148 spells qualify.
design.power: Not adequately powered at 11 cases. A minimum viable test would need a pre-specified minimum detectable effect and an estimate of the number of cases required. Without that, the study is descriptive only.
design.controls: Pre-absence usage baseline and regression-to-the-mean correction using matched non-absence stretches for the same player. Minutes, starter status, lineup, and opponent controls. Profile computed only from games strictly before absence start. Label derivation fixed before outcome computation.
design.falsification: Placebo absences: randomly chosen windows in which the player was present, with the same procedure applied. If placebo cases show similar largest-gainer patterns, the effect is not specific to absence.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one comparator and one primary play type per absent player. All other comparators and play types are secondary and descriptive only. Apply a correction across the secondary tests.
design.decision_rule: Support requires the pre-registered closest-profile teammate to be the largest gainer in the pre-specified primary play types in more cases than the placebo rate, with a confidence interval excluding zero, after regression-to-the-mean correction. Otherwise report uncertain or rejected as appropriate. Report untestable if the power analysis shows the minimum detectable effect is not reached.
design.data_version: Snapshot as of 2026-11-01. Use the 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, and the 2025-26 regular season only after it is complete (2026-04-13). Exclude the 2025-26 playoffs unless complete (2026-06-21). Record the snapshot date and the label derivation version.
